record.one_liner: Amazon Selling Partner API: programmatic access to seller and vendor data and operations on Amazon marketplaces.
record.auth_notes: Public apps use OAuth 2.0 via Login with Amazon (LWA). Private apps are self-authorized from Developer Central, which generates an LWA refresh token. No api_key or basic method found in the fetched pages.
record.access_notes: critic: confirmed paid_plan. Developer Central and SP-API integration require a Professional selling account ($39.99/month + selling fees); no free or trial path to credentials found on the vendor page.
record.api_notes: critic: api_breadth moderate -> broad; the docs index lists many API families (FBA, Vendor Direct Fulfillment, Vendor Retail Procurement, Warehousing and Distribution, Application Management, plus orders, listings, pricing, etc.). REST style inferred from HTTP/LWA access-token model; not stated explicitly.
record.blocker_notes: critic: confirmed. A Professional selling account at $39.99/month plus selling fees is required before creating an SP-API developer profile. Official MCP (Amazon org, local npm package) exists.

evidence.quote: Public applications must use OAuth 2.0 to obtain authorization from selling partners to call the SP-API on the selling partner's behalf.
The self-authorization process generates an LWA refresh token.
Yes, only Professional selling accounts can access Developer Central and integrate with SP-API.
A Professional selling account is $39.99/month + selling fees.
An LWA access token must be included in calls to all operations except restricted operations, which return Personally Identifiable Information (PII).
Local MCP for SP-API brings this to the SP-API ecosystem as a consolidated npm package bundling MCP servers for Amazon Selling Partner API development.
You must have a Professional selling account and be the primary account user to create an SP-API developer profile.

input.query: Amazon Selling Partner API MCP server
